item.title: [1/3] AI 2040: Plan A report - Daniel Kokotajlo & Thomas Larsen — Machine Learning Street Talk (MLST)
item.description:
Edition: 2026-09-10 — Frontier pacing, open infrastructure and the workflow bottleneck
Why it matters: Start with the hardest strategic question of the week: whether frontier AI development should be deliberately slowed, what a credible pause would actually buy, and where the AI 2040 Plan A proposal is robust or speculative. MLST's long-form format is useful here because it pushes beyond slogans into assumptions about takeoff speed, control, coordination and governance.
Source: Machine Learning Street Talk (MLST) Original publication: 2026-09-08T11:27:44Z

item.title: [2/3] How Open-Source is Reshaping the AI Infrastructure Stack — The Enterprise AI Show
item.description:
Edition: 2026-09-10 — Frontier pacing, open infrastructure and the workflow bottleneck
Why it matters: Move from frontier governance to the stack beneath enterprise AI. David Aronchick brings unusually relevant infrastructure experience from Kubernetes, Kubeflow and Azure; the useful lens is where open models and open infrastructure create durable leverage, where hyperscaler economics still dominate, and what enterprises should actually own versus rent.
Source: The Enterprise AI Show Original publication: 2026-09-09T05:00:00Z

item.title: [3/3] Fast AI. Slow workflow. — AI Infrastructure
item.description:
Edition: 2026-09-10 — Frontier pacing, open infrastructure and the workflow bottleneck
Why it matters: Finish at the operational layer. Faster inference and stronger coding agents do not automatically accelerate delivery when approvals, context gathering, repository complexity, debugging and human coordination remain serial bottlenecks. This is the practical counterweight to benchmark-driven narratives about AI productivity.
Source: AI Infrastructure Original publication: 2026-09-09T10:13:27Z

item.title: [1/4] The rise and fall of agent civilizations — Dwarkesh Podcast
item.description:
Edition: 2026-09-03 — Agents, architecture, compute and assurance
Why it matters: Start here for the capability shift. A compact account of what happened when many coding agents were allowed to operate together, what emergent coordination looked like, where the system failed, and why multi-agent security now deserves to be treated as an engineering problem rather than science fiction.
Source: Dwarkesh Podcast Original publication: 2026-08-31T20:36:53Z

item.title: [2/4] Less about Models; More about Architecture — Practical AI
item.description:
Edition: 2026-09-03 — Agents, architecture, compute and assurance
Why it matters: The enterprise reality check. The useful question is increasingly not which model wins a benchmark, but how models are wrapped in architecture, context, tools, data, evaluation and controls. This is a good bridge from frontier capability to deployable systems.
Source: Practical AI Original publication: 2026-09-03T09:00:00Z

item.title: [3/4] Redefining Chip Architecture with Arm CEO Rene Haas — No Priors: Artificial Intelligence | Technology | Startups
item.description:
Edition: 2026-09-03 — Agents, architecture, compute and assurance
Why it matters: The compute layer beneath the model race. Focus on how AI changes CPU and data-center architecture, Arm's move beyond pure IP licensing, supply-chain constraints, hyperscaler demand and where economic power may shift as inference scales.
Source: No Priors: Artificial Intelligence | Technology | Startups Original publication: 2026-09-03T10:00:00Z

item.title: [4/4] Building AI Assurance Ecosystem with Bri Treece (PACT AI) and Dr. Rob Slone (UL Solutions) — Scaling Laws
item.description:
Edition: 2026-09-03 — Agents, architecture, compute and assurance
Why it matters: Regulation only matters if institutions can measure and verify systems. This gets concrete about assurance, continuous evaluation, standards, independent testing and the missing infrastructure between high-level AI rules and real-world enforcement.
Source: Scaling Laws Original publication: 2026-09-01T09:00:00Z
